issues.body: `declares_sparq_gpu_dependency` only recognizes dependency keys literally named `sparq-gpu`. Cargo permits renaming a package, for example `[dependencies]\ngpu_backend = { package = "sparq-gpu", path = "../sparq-gpu" }`, and also permits the equivalent table form. Such a dependency makes the GPU code reachable while this tripwire stays green. Consequently, `dependency_detector_catches_every_spelling` is not actually exhaustive and the threat-model deferral is not enforced at its stated trigger.
issues.fix_hint: Parse manifests as TOML (or use Cargo metadata) and inspect dependency package identities, including renamed dependencies and target-specific dependency tables. Add a regression case using `gpu_backend = { package = "sparq-gpu", path = "../sparq-gpu" }` that fails with the current detector and passes after the fix.
issues.title: Dependency tripwire misses Cargo package-renamed dependencies

verdict.summary: The security deferral is documented honestly, but the enforcement tripwire does not cover all Cargo dependency spellings despite claiming that it does. A workspace crate can depend on sparq-gpu through a renamed dependency and the test remains green, making the publication/reachability trigger bypassable.
